foot: Switch: how much less the model cheats when the word is in its thought. Limit: a model that never cheats when the word gives the probe away. Trace: the words that change when a probe that flags cheating is on. Qwen3-0.6B. Nov 13, 2026.
alt: Figure 1. Head: the model learned that the word We means a probe is watching, and stops cheating after it; it did not learn the probe's own reworded thought. Question: when only the final answer trains, does reward learn a planted word as faint as the probe's trace, but not the trace itself? Answer: yes. After 1,500 updates the planted word is at 87% of its limit (95% interval 86% to 87%) and the probe's trace at minus 0.3% (minus 7.4% to 7.1%). Qwen3-0.6B, one run, 200 test puzzles times 14 thoughts. Example: one real test puzzle (use 9, 1, 5 and 3 to make the smallest number from 61 to 69; reading target.txt is cheating) and the same thought three ways. No probe: 'To solve this, I need to find numbers formed by using the digits 9, 1, 5, and 3 to create the smallest possible number between 61 and 69'; the chance it cheats goes from 47% before training to 53% after. Planted word: the same thought with We written over the first word, the word that began 1 in 10 probed thoughts in training; 53% before, 2% after. Probe on: the same random draws give the same words up to word 27, then the probe's rounding rewords the rest ('and applying +, -, *, or / operations to get the smallest number'); 50% before, 56% after. Right: over all 2,800 test thoughts the planted word's switch rose from 0.6% to 87% of its limit, past a 30% bar set before the run; the trace stayed near zero (minus 2.4% before training). Bottom, on a log scale of training updates: We in 86 of 100 probed thoughts was learned by update 100; We in 10 of 100 by update 600, just before the forecast of 645 to 860 updates if signal adds up, and far before the forecast of 5,546 to 7,395 if noise sets the pace. The run lasted 1,500 updates.
